_metadata.verified_2026_05_13: BPM120 mesh investigation complete. TWO independent levers: (1) cells_per_diameter for bulk uniform refinement (cpd=15→246K, cpd=30→1.17M, cpd=40→2.22M), and (2) surfaceRefinementLevels for near-wall refinement (cpd=15+[1,2]→246K, cpd=15+[2,3]→1.10M — 4.5x more cells with no cpd change). config_paper_reference.json uses lever (2): cpd=15 + surfaceRefinementLevels=[2,3] → 1.10M cells. Mesh character matters: [2,3] puts cells in the boundary layer where WSS sensitivity lives, vs. cpd-only which distributes cells uniformly in the bulk. The paper says '~1.9M cells' without specifying mesh character — 1.10M with the right character is more useful than 2.22M with the wrong character.

production_standard._comment: Wang et al. Table 3 reference. Cell-count range reflects what current code actually produces (246K legacy / 317K adaptive_span); paper's 1.9M unverified on this codebase.

osi_mean_masked._comment: value pending; placeholder for tolerance shape

production_standard._mesh_note: Reproduce via cases_input/BPM120/config_paper_reference.json (cpd=15 + surfaceRefinementLevels=[2,3], verified 1.10M cells 2026-05-13). Default config.json uses cpd=15 + [1,2] (~246K cells) for fast onboarding and is NOT the paper reference. Slightly below paper's 1.9M cell-count claim but the more physically meaningful interpretation — coarse bulk + fine near walls, vs. earlier cpd=40 attempt which gave 2.22M uniformly-finer cells (wrong character for WSS-sensitive geometry).

production_robust._comment: First-order schemes give a sharper resolved coarctation peak → ~27% higher TAWSS p99 than standard. Pressure drop ~4% lower. Per Wang et al. Table 3 scheme-sensitivity.
